selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: Why does the note say some topics from other books of the Risale-i Nur appear again in this treatise?
questions.answer: Because the other parts were not available where this treatise was being written, so some important points had to be included here too.

questions.question: Which works are named as containing some of the important matters mentioned again here?
questions.answer: The Words and The Flashes.

questions.question: What educational benefit did the writer want for the local students?
questions.answer: He wanted them to write out a miniature complete Risale-i Nur.

questions.question: After the explanation about repetition, what new subject does the note move to?
questions.answer: It moves to the revised copy and a meaningful number pattern in it.

questions.question: What detail makes the writer think the pattern in the copy was not just planned by human skill?
questions.answer: The copyist was not knowledgeable in these special subjects.

questions.question: What hidden order was found in his copy?
questions.answer: The line openings contained 666 alifs.

questions.question: What conclusion is drawn from this number matching the title?
questions.answer: It is taken as a sign that the title fits the treatise well.

questions.question: What belief about the treatise comes from this numerical harmony?
questions.answer: That the title suits it and that the treatise has a special connection to Qur’anic light.

questions.question: What second layer of meaning is found in the same number pattern?
questions.answer: It also points to the treatise being linked to the light of the Qur’an’s verses.

questions.question: If a student asked for the central lesson of the note, what would be a good answer?
questions.answer: The note teaches that the treatise was preserved for a real need and that its writing showed signs the author saw as meaningful and Qur’an-related.

questions.question: What problem in that location made it necessary to include some material again in this treatise?
questions.answer: The other sections of the Risale-i Nur were not there.

questions.question: What was that reason?
questions.answer: Important subjects had to be included because the other related books were unavailable there.

questions.question: What does the phrase about writing a “complete” small Risale-i Nur suggest about this treatise?
questions.answer: It suggests the treatise was meant to help gather essential teachings in one accessible form.

questions.question: Who produced the revised version of the draft?
questions.answer: A blessed person did.

questions.question: How is the person who made that revised copy described in both spiritual and educational terms?
questions.answer: He is described as blessed, but not trained in those technical matters.

questions.question: Why is the number 666 important in the note?
questions.answer: It matches the abjad value of the title Ayat al-Kubra.

questions.question: Which title is said to have the same number value as the counted alifs?
questions.answer: Ayat al-Kubra, or The Supreme Sign.

questions.question: What two things are linked by this number in the note?
questions.answer: The title Ayat al-Kubra and the number of verses of the Qur’an.

questions.question: What spiritual meaning is then added to this numerical agreement?
questions.answer: It is taken as a sign that the treatise comes as a gleam from the Qur’an.

questions.question: What is one strong theme running through the whole note?
questions.answer: The treatise is shown as both carefully preserved and spiritually meaningful.

questions.question: According to the note, was the repetition in the treatise presented as careless writing or as something done for a reason?
questions.answer: It was presented as something done for a reason.

questions.question: What made those other parts unusable in that situation?
questions.answer: They were not present in the place where this treatise was composed.

questions.question: What was the purpose of having students write down the whole treatise?
questions.answer: The purpose was to let them produce a shortened but complete collection of the Risale-i Nur.

questions.question: What happened after the rough draft stage?
questions.answer: A revised copy was made.
